text:
The Devils arrive on a three-game winning streak, the latest a 5-4 overtime win over STL that Jesper Bratt won, and they are 4-1-0 in their last five. The Islanders are 2-3-0 over the same stretch after a 5-3 home loss to CAR, and they're playing without Ryan Pulock, Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie. There is also a rematch: NYI won the Oct. 3 meeting 6-0, though by chances NJD was the better side that night in expected-goals terms (we had NYI deserving to win just 44% of the time).

Our numbers favor NJD in how the games are played. At five on five the Devils have taken 59% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) to NYI's 50%, and they've been better than their record: a +9 goal difference on +17.8 expected. NJD's power play creates 0.79 expected goals a game against a penalty kill allowing 0.86, and NYI takes 4.5 penalties a game. The goalie matchup is the one place NYI has the edge. Projected starter Ilya Sorokin is +5.6 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shots predict) after +22.3 last season. Jake Allen is at -4.0 this season, though +5.4 last year. With Maccelli out, Bo Horvat has moved beside Cizikas and Holmstrom, and Simon Holmstrom is up to 20:55 a night.

Jack Hughes is our top pick to score at 40% and to reach two points. Hughes and Arseny Gritsyuk are tied for the Devils' goal lead with 8. For NYI, Horvat is at 36% to score. Matthew Schaefer, the 2025 first overall pick, is our best bet at 28% for two or more points.
